requirement_text.REQ-070: Router decomposition into per-subsystem sub-routers (OQ-1). Acceptance criteria: (AC1) GET /health 200+{"status":"ok"} no auth/DB; (AC2) sub-router isolation test; (AC3) unrouted path returns RFC 9457 404 with Content-Type: application/problem+json; (AC4) single shared middleware declaration site grep-verified; (AC5) moduledoc lists all 11 deferred routes with stages; (AC6) moduledoc cites REQ-065 addendum by name.

task.description:
WF-02 Step 3b — HARD GATE: Validate TEST-DESIGNER's test coverage for REQ-070.

Read test/letflow/router_test.exs and test/specs/REQ-070.md directly. Do NOT rely on TEST-DESIGNER's summary.

For each acceptance criterion, verify a runnable test exists:

AC1 (GET /health, no DB): Is there a test that calls GET /health via Plug.Test WITHOUT starting Ecto.Sandbox? Does it assert status 200 AND body == {"status":"ok"}?

AC2 (sub-router isolation): Is there a test that mounts a sub-router (e.g. Letflow.Routers.Identity) directly via Plug.Test without going through the top-level router? Does it call call/2 on the sub-router module directly?

AC3 (RFC 9457 404): Is there a test that calls an unrouted path on the top-level router? Does it assert BOTH (a) Content-Type contains "application/problem+json" AND (b) the body contains RFC 9457 keys (type/title/status/detail or equivalent from lib/letflow/api/error.ex)? Does it verify the body does NOT have the old {"error":"not_found"} shape?

AC4 (single middleware site): Is there a test that verifies Plug.Parsers and AuthPipeline each appear in exactly one file in lib/? Does it use the invocation-form string (not just the module name, since the module name appears in type annotations and imports)?

AC5 (moduledoc deferred routes): Is there a test that reads lib/letflow/router.ex as text and asserts all 11 deferred route names appear?

AC6 (moduledoc addendum citation): Is there a test that asserts the file contains the addendum date or document name?

Additional checks:
- No shared/destructive state across tests (each test is independent)
- No hardcoded secrets or connection strings in the test file
- Test names match the AC numbers they cover (makes failures readable)
- mix compile --warnings-as-errors confirmed passing with these tests

FAIL immediately on any missed AC. No partial credit for 'mostly covered'.

Complete the handoff: status COMPLETED, result.status PASS or FAIL. On FAIL: list each missed AC in result.issues at BLOCKER severity, next_action 'Rework TEST-DESIGNER (Step 3 rework)'. On PASS: next_action 'Route to TEST-RUNNER (Step 4)'. Commit the completed handoff on branch feature/WF02-REQ070-20260821 by explicit path.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 6 ACs has at least one runnable test
AC1 test does not use Ecto.Sandbox
AC2 test calls a sub-router module directly without the top-level router
AC3 test asserts both Content-Type header and RFC 9457 body shape
AC4 test uses invocation-form string search (not bare module name)

result.summary: All 6 ACs verified against test/letflow/router_test.exs and lib/letflow/api/error.ex directly. AC1: ExUnit.Case async:true, no Ecto.Sandbox anywhere, asserts status 200 + body {status:ok}. AC2: Letflow.Routers.Identity.call(@identity_opts) called directly with no top-level router involved. AC3: Content-Type assertion present; Map.has_key? checks type/title/status/detail match error.ex serialise/1 output; old {error:not_found} shape excluded by exact-equality @not_found_body assertion in pre-existing test. AC4: invocation-form strings plug(Plug.Parsers, and plug(Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline) used (not bare names); both assert length==1 and hd =~ api_pipeline. AC5: all 11 fully-qualified Letflow.Routers.* names asserted; 'not ported' asserted separately. AC6: '0001-web-framework.md' and '2026-08-20' both asserted. No @tag :skip, no TODO stubs, no shared state, no secrets.
